text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A British spokesman for NATO-led SFOR troops tells Vjesnik there was no British military action to capture war criminals in central Bosnia last week.
- U.S. human rights envoy John Shattuck told Croatian mothers of the disappeared in Zagreb that America would not rest until all those responsible for mass killings are brought to justice.
- Association of Widows says the law on welfare for children whose fathers were killed in the 1991 war is not being applied in practice.
- Some 500 drivers have their driving licences taken by the police for drunk driving every weekend.
- More and more incidents in Kistanje, southern Croatia, between Serbs who returned to the village this year and newly resettled Croats from Yugoslavia.
- Aftermath of soccer match between Croatia, Zagreb and Partizan, Belgrade - Partizan punished Croatia's failures to score.
- After several Croatian Army generals were dimissed or retired - young officers are being promoted and experienced senior officers with war experience climb to the top.
- Speed boats - a threat to swimmers. More care is needed this year, when Croatia expects some 150,000 vessels to sail in the Adriatic.
- Posters of Dario Kordic, a Bosnian Croat indicted by the International War Crimes Tribunal, have sprung up all over Busovaca in central Bosnia as a sign of support for Bosnian Croats.
- I believe financial results so far can guarantee there will not have to be changes to the 1997 budget estimate, says Finance Minister Bozo Prka.
- Fear and hope in Zagreb, after Croatia lost first match with Partizan Belgrade 0-1. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
